bodies.intuition: Attention borrows its vocabulary from databases. Each position emits a query — what am I looking for — and every position also offers a key, advertising what it has. Queries and keys are matched to decide where to look; the value is what actually gets read once the match is made. Splitting the three lets a position advertise something different from what it delivers.
bodies.engineer: Three learned projections of the same input: Q = XW_Q, K = XW_K, V = XW_V. Keys and queries must share a dimension because they are dotted together; values need not, and their dimension sets the output width. Separating K from V is what lets the model be found for one reason and read for another, which a single shared projection cannot express.
bodies.math: For input X ∈ ℝ^{n×d_model}, W_Q, W_K ∈ ℝ^{d_model×d_k} and W_V ∈ ℝ^{d_model×d_v}. In self-attention all three project the same X; in cross-attention Q comes from one sequence and K, V from another. The parameter cost is d_model·(2d_k + d_v) per head.

emphasis.intuition: advertise something different from what it delivers
emphasis.engineer: found for one reason and read for another
